## S3.3 Functional GEE {#sec-s4-fgee}

```{r s5-setup}
s5_read <- \(f) readr::read_csv(file.path("competitors/fgee/summaries", f), show_col_types = FALSE)
s5_A <- s5_read("A-pooled.csv")
s5_As <- s5_read("A-summary.csv")
# Width and interval score relative to REML + CL2 in the same setting
s5_rel <- \(x) {
  ref <- x |>
    filter(method == "reml_cl2") |>
    select(cell, estimand, w_cl2 = width, s_cl2 = interval_score)
  x |>
    left_join(ref, by = c("cell", "estimand"), relationship = "many-to-one") |>
    mutate(wr = width / w_cl2, sr = interval_score / s_cl2)
}
s5_B <- s5_read("B-summary.csv") |> mutate(dep = error != "iid") |> s5_rel()
s5_BP <- s5_read("B-paired-ncv-summary.csv") |> mutate(dep = error != "iid")
s5_P <- bind_rows(s5_read("P-summary.csv"), s5_read("cardio/P-summary.csv")) |> s5_rel()
s5_PP <- bind_rows(s5_read("P-paired-ncv-summary.csv"), s5_read("cardio/Pc-paired-ncv-summary.csv"))
s5_P_ALL <- c(running = 90, dti = 92, gait_vc = 138, ecg_roahd = 100, ecg_gls4b = 78, af = 118)
s5_P <- s5_P |> mutate(all_subjects = G == s5_P_ALL[app])
# Critical values of the calibrated intervals for beta and the mean
s5_Bc <- s5_read("B-crit.csv") |> left_join(distinct(s5_B, cell, dep, G), by = "cell")
s5_Pc <- bind_rows(s5_read("P-crit.csv"), s5_read("cardio/P-crit.csv")) |>
  left_join(distinct(s5_P, cell, app, all_subjects), by = "cell")
s5_bc <- \(est, dep, col, g = c(40, 100), base = "fgee_independent")
  s5_Bc[[col]][s5_Bc$estimand %in% est & s5_Bc$dep %in% dep & s5_Bc$G %in% g & s5_Bc$base %in% base]
s5_pc <- \(est, all_subj, col, apps = names(s5_P_ALL), base = "fgee_independent")
  s5_Pc[[col]][s5_Pc$estimand %in% est & s5_Pc$all_subjects %in% all_subj & s5_Pc$app %in% apps & s5_Pc$base %in% base]
s5_t_floor <- qt(0.975, 1) / qnorm(0.975)
# REML + CL2 with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, beta (same cell numbers and data sets)
s5_satt <- readr::read_csv("satterthwaite/summaries/satt-cells.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(crit == "satt", estimand == "beta") |>
  select(cell, cov_satt = coverage, q05_satt = pointwise_q05, w_satt = width)
# Fitted means: the summary files scale non-Gaussian mean widths differently, so the Satterthwaite
# factor is taken within satt-cells.csv and applied to the width ratio against the normal critical value
s5_satt_mean <- readr::read_csv("satterthwaite/summaries/satt-cells.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(crit %in% c("z", "satt"), estimand == "mean") |>
  select(cell, crit, coverage, width) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = crit, values_from = c(coverage, width))
s5_mean_satt <- \(m) s5_B |>
  filter(method == m, estimand == "mean", dep) |>
  left_join(s5_satt_mean, by = "cell", relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  mutate(wr_satt = wr * width_z / width_satt)
s5_vs_satt <- s5_B |>
  filter(method == "fgee_independent_wildL", estimand == "beta", dep) |>
  left_join(s5_satt, by = "cell", relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  mutate(wr_satt = width / w_satt)

# Experiment A: pooled coverage over the three coefficient functions
s5_a <- \(m, ni = c(1, 5), n = c(25, 100, 500), fam = c("gaussian", "poisson", "binomial"))
  s5_A$coverage[s5_A$method %in% m & s5_A$n_i %in% ni & s5_A$N %in% n & s5_A$family %in% fam]
s5_as <- \(m, est, col, n = c(25, 100, 500)) s5_As[[col]][s5_As$method %in% m & s5_As$estimand %in% est & s5_As$N %in% n]
s5_conv <- s5_A |>
  filter(method %in% c("fgee_base_fixed", "refund_cr_freq_centred")) |>
  select(cell, family, method, coverage) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = coverage) |>
  mutate(d = abs(fgee_base_fixed - refund_cr_freq_centred))
s5_cl2_low <- s5_As |> filter(method == "refund_cl2") |> slice_min(coverage, n = 1)

# Experiment B
s5_b <- \(m, est, dep, col = "coverage", g = c(40, 100))
  s5_B[[col]][s5_B$method %in% m & s5_B$estimand %in% est & s5_B$dep %in% dep & s5_B$G %in% g]
s5_bp <- \(ct, e, d) s5_BP |> filter(contrast == .env$ct, estimand %in% .env$e, dep %in% .env$d)

# Plasmode
s5_p <- \(m, est, col = "coverage", apps = names(s5_P_ALL), all_subj = c(TRUE, FALSE))
  s5_P[[col]][s5_P$method %in% m & s5_P$estimand %in% est & s5_P$app %in% apps & s5_P$all_subjects %in% all_subj]
s5_pp <- \(ct, e) s5_PP |> filter(contrast == .env$ct, estimand %in% .env$e)

s5_labels <- c(
  reml_model = "REML, model-based",
  reml_cl2 = "REML + CL2",
  fgee_independent = "fGEE, independence",
  fgee_ar1 = "fGEE, AR(1)",
  fgee_fpca = "fGEE, FPCA",
  fgee_independent_wild = "fGEE, independence, calibrated crit.",
  fgee_ar1_wild = "fGEE, AR(1), calibrated crit.",
  fgee_fpca_wild = "fGEE, FPCA, calibrated crit.",
  fgee_independent_wildL = "fGEE, independence, calibrated crit.",
  fgee_independent_wildL_noT = "fGEE, independence, calibrated crit. without t",
  fgee_ar1_wildL = "fGEE, AR(1), calibrated crit.",
  fgee_ar1_wildL_noT = "fGEE, AR(1), calibrated crit. without t",
  fgee_fpca_wildL = "fGEE, FPCA, calibrated crit.",
  fgee_fpca_wildL_noT = "fGEE, FPCA, calibrated crit. without t"
)
# Calibrated intervals for beta and the mean: critical value with and without the t adjustment
s5_ind_cal <- "fgee_independent_wildL"
s5_ind_not <- "fgee_independent_wildL_noT"
s5_all_cal <- paste0("fgee_", c("independent", "ar1", "fpca"), "_wildL")
s5_all_not <- paste0(s5_all_cal, "_noT")
s5_estimands <- c(beta = "β(s,t)", mean = "mean (link)", alpha = "α(t)", gamma = "γ(t)")
s5_apps <- c(ecg_gls4b = "ECG strain", af = "AF trial", running = "running", dti = "DTI",
  gait_vc = "gait", ecg_roahd = "ECG 8-lead")
```

### Simulation design of the functional GEE paper

We reran the function-on-scalar simulation of @LoewingerLevisCuiPereira2025 [Section 4] with
their data generator unchanged: $Y_{ij}(s) = \beta_0(s) + X_{1i}\beta_1(s) + X_{2i}\beta_2(s) + \varepsilon_{ij}(s)$
(in their notation, $j$ indexes the curves of subject $i$ and $s$ the grid)
on 50 grid points, with Gaussian errors (variance 10) or Poisson and binary responses generated
through a Gaussian copula whose latent correlation is AR(1) (0.75) along $s$ and exchangeable
(0.75) between the curves of a subject. The design crosses the three families with
`r knitr::combine_words(sort(unique(s5_A$N)), and = " or ")` subjects and
`r paste(sort(unique(s5_A$n_i), decreasing = TRUE), collapse = " or ")` curves per subject
(`r max(s5_A$n_i)` as in their study, `r min(s5_A$n_i)` as in ours), with
`r max(s5_A$R)` replicates per setting; `r plural(sum(s5_A$R < max(s5_A$R) & !grepl("_wild$", s5_A$method)), "one-step fit")` failed
(singular system). The initial fit is their pffr call (bam with fREML,
discretization, P-spline bases with 16 functions); all intervals labeled "initial fit" in
@tbl-s4-fgee-a are computed on that fit, the REML row on a refit of the same model and bases by gam
with REML, and all clusters are subjects.

Every interval is scored through
one evaluation matrix per coefficient function; these matrices reproduce fastFGEE's fitted curves
and standard errors, so centering and basis differences between methods do not enter. As in their
Table 3, coverage is the pointwise 95% coverage averaged over the grid, over replicates and over
$\beta_0$, $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$; its Monte Carlo standard error is at most
`r f(max(s5_A$coverage_mc_se), 3)`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s4-fgee-a
#| tbl-cap: "Simulation design of the functional GEE paper: ranges over the nine settings (three families, three numbers of subjects) of the coverage of nominal 95% pointwise intervals, averaged over the grid and the three coefficient functions, by number of curves per subject. Initial fit: the pffr call of that paper (bam). fGEE: one-step update with the stated functional and longitudinal working correlations. Calibrated crit.: fastFGEE's wild-bootstrap critical value with its t adjustment; z: normal critical value."
s5_a_methods <- c(
  model = "Initial fit, model-based",
  fgee_base = "Initial-fit sandwich of fastFGEE, z",
  fgee_base_wild = "Initial-fit sandwich of fastFGEE, calibrated crit.",
  fgee_base_fixed = "Initial-fit sandwich of fastFGEE, penalty rescaled, z",
  refund_cr_freq_centred = "Initial fit, cluster sandwich, frequentist, centered scores",
  refund_cr = "Initial fit, CR1",
  refund_cl2 = "Initial fit, CL2",
  reml_cl2 = "REML (gam) fit, CL2",
  fgee_independent_independent = "fGEE, independence × independence, z",
  fgee_independent_independent_wild = "fGEE, independence × independence, calibrated crit.",
  fgee_ar1_exchangeable = "fGEE, AR(1) × exchangeable, z",
  fgee_ar1_exchangeable_wild = "fGEE, AR(1) × exchangeable, calibrated crit."
)
s5_A |>
  filter(method %in% names(s5_a_methods)) |>
  group_by(method, n_i) |>
  summarise(r = rng(coverage), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = n_i, values_from = r) |>
  mutate(method = factor(method, names(s5_a_methods))) |>
  arrange(method) |>
  mutate(method = s5_a_methods[as.character(method)]) |>
  select(method, `5`, `1`) |>
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "",
    col.names = c("Intervals", "5 curves per subject", "1 curve per subject"))
```

With `r max(s5_A$n_i)` curves per subject, CL2 clustered by subject on the initial fit covers
`r rng(s5_a("refund_cl2", 5, c(100, 500)))` with 100 or 500 subjects and
`r rng(s5_a("refund_cl2", 5, 25))` with 25. Refitting by gam and REML changes the pooled CL2
coverage by at most
`r f(max(abs(s5_a("refund_cl2") - s5_a("reml_cl2"))), 3)`. The intervals of fastFGEE's functional GEE
(fGEE), a one-step update of the initial fit under the stated working correlations, with its
calibrated critical values cover `r rng(s5_a(c("fgee_independent_independent_wild", "fgee_ar1_exchangeable_wild"), 5))`
in this design; with a normal critical value, they cover
`r rng(s5_a(c("fgee_independent_independent", "fgee_ar1_exchangeable"), 5, c(25, 100)))` with
at most 100 subjects and `r rng(s5_a(c("fgee_independent_independent", "fgee_ar1_exchangeable"), 5, 500))`
with 500. The one-step estimate of $\beta_1$ has a root-mean-square error of
`r rng(s5_as("fgee_independent_independent", "beta1", "rmse") / s5_as("refund_cl2", "beta1", "rmse"))`
(independence) and
`r rng(s5_as("fgee_ar1_exchangeable", "beta1", "rmse") / s5_as("refund_cl2", "beta1", "rmse"))`
(AR(1) × exchangeable) times that of the initial fit.

### The initial-fit sandwich and penalty-scale conventions

mgcv's smoothing parameters are on the scale of the summed log-likelihood: the penalized
estimate maximizes $\sum_{i=1}^n \ell_i(\boldsymbol\theta) - \boldsymbol\theta^\top\mathbf S_{\boldsymbol\lambda}\boldsymbol\theta/(2\phi)$,
with $\mathbf S_{\boldsymbol\lambda} = \sum_r \lambda_r \mathbf S_r$, $n$ clusters (subjects) and the sum over
all observations of cluster $i$ in $\ell_i$ (for the Gaussian, the residual sum of squares).
A sandwich written with averaged quantities therefore needs the bread
$$
\bar{\mathbf A} = \frac1n \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf X_i^\top \mathbf W_i \mathbf X_i + \frac{\mathbf S_{\boldsymbol\lambda}}{n\phi}
= (n\,\mathbf V_p)^{-1},
$$
with $\mathbf W_i$ the Fisher weights of the main text, and
$\bar{\mathbf A}^{-1}\bar{\mathbf M}\bar{\mathbf A}^{-1}/n$ with the averaged meat $\bar{\mathbf M}$
is then the cluster sandwich $\mathbf V_p(\sum_i \mathbf U_i\mathbf U_i^\top)\mathbf V_p$ up to
degrees-of-freedom factors.

The initial-fit sandwich of fastFGEE 0.2.2 (`gee.fit = FALSE`), which the simulation code of
@LoewingerLevisCuiPereira2025 calls for their pffr baseline, differs in the penalty scale: it adds
$\mathbf S_{\boldsymbol\lambda}$ to the averaged bread, a penalty larger by the factor $n\phi$
(for the Gaussian, approximately $n\sigma^2$). The estimate is the unchanged pffr estimate, but the
inverse bread, and with it the standard errors, shrink. In their design, the ratio of mean
standard error to the empirical standard deviation of $\hat\beta_1$ is
`r rng(s5_as("fgee_base", "beta1", "se_sd_ratio"))` for this sandwich and does not improve with the
number of subjects (`r rng(s5_as("fgee_base", "beta1", "se_sd_ratio", 25))` with 25,
`r rng(s5_as("fgee_base", "beta1", "se_sd_ratio", 500))` with 500), because the penalty-scale
difference does not vanish.

With `r max(s5_A$n_i)` curves per subject, its pooled coverage is
`r rng(s5_a("fgee_base", 5, fam = "gaussian"))` for Gaussian,
`r rng(s5_a("fgee_base", 5, fam = "poisson"))` for Poisson and
`r rng(s5_a("fgee_base", 5, fam = "binomial"))` for binary responses (@tbl-s4-fgee-a); its coverage here is in
line with their Table 3 for the pffr baseline. With its wild-bootstrap critical value, which widens the
intervals instead, coverage is `r rng(s5_a("fgee_base_wild", 5, c(100, 500)))` with 100 or more
subjects.

Dividing the penalty by $n\phi$ and leaving everything else unchanged gives pooled coverage of
`r rng(s5_a("fgee_base_fixed"))` over all `r nrow(s5_conv)` settings. The rescaled sandwich then
coincides with refund's frequentist cluster sandwich (no $\mathbf V_p - \mathbf V_e$ term) with
centered cluster scores: pooled coverages `r if (max(s5_conv$d[s5_conv$family != "gaussian"]) < 5e-4) "agree to three decimals" else "differ"` in every Poisson and binary setting and differ by at most
`r f(max(s5_conv$d), 3)` in the Gaussian settings, where fastFGEE estimates the working variance per
grid point instead of using one $\sigma^2$.

CL2 on the same fit covers
`r rng(s5_a("refund_cl2", n = c(100, 500)))` with 100 or 500 subjects and
`r rng(s5_a("refund_cl2", n = 25))` with 25; the lowest single coefficient function is
`r f(s5_cl2_low$coverage, 2)` ($\beta_`r sub("beta", "", s5_cl2_low$estimand)`$,
`r c(gaussian = "Gaussian", poisson = "Poisson", binomial = "binary")[s5_cl2_low$family]`,
`r s5_cl2_low$N` subjects, `r s5_cl2_low$n_i` curve per subject). Its gain over the rescaled sandwich at
25 subjects, `r rng(s5_a("refund_cl2", n = 25) - s5_a("fgee_base_fixed", n = 25), 3)`, combines
uncentered scores, the $\mathbf V_p - \mathbf V_e$ term and the leverage adjustment.

### The main factorial settings of our simulation

fastFGEE was started from the REML fit of the main study in its 18 main factorial settings at the default
signal level (Gaussian, Poisson and binary responses; independent, rough stationary and smooth errors;
$G = 40$ and 100; model $\mathrm{ff}(X) + z\gamma(t)$; one curve per subject;
`r min(s5_B$R)` replicates, the main study's datasets), with curves as clusters, independent
longitudinal correlation, functional working correlation independence, AR(1) or FPCA, and the
package defaults otherwise (cluster cross-validation of the smoothing parameters, wild bootstrap).

We score Wald intervals from its covariance with the normal critical value and intervals with its
calibrated critical value (studentized wild cluster bootstrap with $t$ adjustment), both with the
same estimate and standard error. The bootstrap gives one critical value per dataset, a quantile of
the absolute studentized statistics pooled over the evaluation points, so it targets coverage
averaged over these points and not coverage at each point.

The interval interface of fastFGEE covers the
functional intercept and scalar-covariate effects but not $\mathrm{ff}$ surfaces or fitted means. For
$\alpha(t)$ and $\gamma(t)$, we transfer its critical value for the term to our evaluation points; the
calibration on the package's own term grid need not carry over to other points. For $\beta(s,t)$ and
the mean, we call the package's internal bootstrap routine with our evaluation matrix as the linear
map and all other inputs as `fgee()` sets them; with the package's own term maps, this call reproduced
its stored critical values exactly in the settings we checked.

The $t$ adjustment multiplies the
critical value by the ratio of $t$ and normal quantiles, with degrees of freedom equal to the number of
curves minus the effective degrees of freedom of the coefficients the map involves, floored at 1. The
surface and the mean involve many more coefficients than the package's term maps, so, with few
curves, the floor can be reached, where the factor is `r f(s5_t_floor, 2)`. We therefore report these
intervals with and without the adjustment. Monte Carlo standard errors of coverage are at most
`r f(max(s5_B$coverage_mc_se), 3)`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s4-fgee-b
#| tbl-cap: "Main factorial settings of our simulation: ranges of grid-averaged coverage of nominal 95% pointwise intervals over the 12 settings with dependent errors (rough stationary, smooth) and the 6 settings with independent errors, and the ratio SE/SD (grid average of mean standard error over the empirical SD of the estimate) under dependence. fGEE intervals: Wald intervals from its covariance, or with its calibrated critical value (for α and γ transferred from its term grid; for β and the mean from its internal routine, with and without its t adjustment). Mean on the link scale."
s5_B |>
  filter(method %in% names(s5_labels)) |>
  group_by(estimand, method) |>
  summarise(
    cov_dep = rng(coverage[dep]),
    cov_iid = rng(coverage[!dep]),
    sesd_dep = if (grepl("_wild", method[1])) "" else rng(se_sd_ratio[dep]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    estimand = factor(estimand, names(s5_estimands)),
    method = factor(method, names(s5_labels))
  ) |>
  arrange(estimand, method) |>
  mutate(
    estimand = ifelse(duplicated(estimand), "", s5_estimands[as.character(estimand)]),
    method = s5_labels[as.character(method)]
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE,
    linesep = "", col.names = c("Estimand", "Intervals", "Cov. dependent", "Cov. independent", "SE/SD dependent"))
```

The Wald intervals for $\beta$ and the mean use the sandwich covariance fastFGEE 0.2.2 returns for
its one-step estimate under the stated working correlation. Under dependent errors, they cover
$\beta(s,t)$ at
`r rng(s5_b(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "beta", TRUE))` against
`r rng(s5_b("reml_cl2", "beta", TRUE))` for REML + CL2 (@tbl-s4-fgee-b). Smoothing bias alone does not
explain the shortfall: the root mean squared bias of the fGEE surface estimate is
`r rng(s5_b(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "beta", TRUE, "rel_bias"))` of its
empirical standard deviation (REML `r rng(s5_b("reml_cl2", "beta", TRUE, "rel_bias"))`), while
SE/SD is `r rng(s5_b(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "beta", TRUE, "se_sd_ratio"))`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s4-fgee-cal
#| tbl-cap: "Main factorial settings, β(s,t) and the mean (link scale): ranges over settings of grid-averaged coverage of nominal 95% pointwise intervals, of the 5% quantile of pointwise coverage over the grid (q05), and of width and interval score relative to REML + CL2 with the normal critical value in the same setting. fGEE with independence working correlation and its calibrated critical value, with and without its t adjustment."
s5_cal_m <- c(
  reml_cl2 = "REML + CL2",
  fgee_independent_wildL = "fGEE, calibrated",
  fgee_independent_wildL_noT = "fGEE, calibrated without t"
)
s5_B |>
  filter(estimand %in% c("beta", "mean"), method %in% names(s5_cal_m)) |>
  group_by(estimand, dep, G, method) |>
  summarise(
    cov = rng(coverage),
    q05 = rng(pointwise_q05),
    wr = if (method[1] == "reml_cl2") "" else rng(wr),
    sr = if (method[1] == "reml_cl2") "" else rng(sr),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(method = factor(method, names(s5_cal_m))) |>
  arrange(estimand, desc(dep), G, method) |>
  mutate(
    estimand = ifelse(duplicated(estimand), "", s5_estimands[as.character(estimand)]),
    dep = ifelse(dep, "dependent", "independent"),
    method = s5_cal_m[as.character(method)]
  ) |>
  select(estimand, dep, G, method, cov, q05, wr, sr) |>
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "",
    col.names = c("Estimand", "Errors", "G", "Intervals", "Coverage", "q05", "Width", "Interval score"))
```

Under dependent errors, with independence working correlation, the calibrated intervals cover $\beta$
at `r rng(s5_b(s5_ind_cal, "beta", TRUE))` (5% quantile of pointwise coverage
`r rng(s5_b(s5_ind_cal, "beta", TRUE, "pointwise_q05"))`), at
`r rng(s5_b(s5_ind_cal, "beta", TRUE, "wr"))` times the width and
`r rng(s5_b(s5_ind_cal, "beta", TRUE, "sr"))` times the interval score of REML + CL2 with the normal
critical value, which covers `r rng(s5_b("reml_cl2", "beta", TRUE))`
(`r rng(s5_b("reml_cl2", "beta", TRUE, "pointwise_q05"))`; @tbl-s4-fgee-cal). REML + CL2 with Satterthwaite
degrees of freedom covers `r rng(s5_vs_satt$cov_satt)` (`r rng(s5_vs_satt$q05_satt)`), and the calibrated
intervals are `r rng(s5_vs_satt$wr_satt)` times its width.

For fitted means, REML + CL2 with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom covers
`r rng(s5_mean_satt("fgee_independent_wildL_noT")$coverage_satt)`; without the $t$ adjustment, the calibrated
intervals cover `r rng(s5_mean_satt("fgee_independent_wildL_noT")$coverage)` at
`r rng(s5_mean_satt("fgee_independent_wildL_noT")$wr_satt)` times its width, and, with the adjustment, they are
up to `r f(max(s5_mean_satt("fgee_independent_wildL")$wr_satt), 2)` times its width with 40 curves.

The median critical value without the $t$ adjustment is
`r rng(s5_bc("beta", TRUE, "crit_no_t_median"))`, whereas the normal quantile divided by SE/SD is
`r rng(qnorm(0.975) / s5_b("fgee_independent", "beta", TRUE, "se_sd_ratio"))`. Over the three working
correlations, the coverage is `r rng(s5_b(s5_all_cal, "beta", TRUE))` for $\beta$ and
`r rng(s5_b(s5_all_cal, "mean", TRUE))` for the mean, the lowest values for FPCA with 40 curves. Under
independent errors, the intervals with independence working correlation cover $\beta$ at
`r rng(s5_b(s5_ind_cal, "beta", FALSE))`, the lowest values for binary responses, at
`r rng(s5_b(s5_ind_cal, "beta", FALSE, "wr"))` times the width and
`r rng(s5_b(s5_ind_cal, "beta", FALSE, "sr"))` times the interval score of REML + CL2, which covers
`r rng(s5_b("reml_cl2", "beta", FALSE))`.

With independence working correlation, the $t$ adjustment changes the coverage of $\beta$ by at most
`r f(max(abs(s5_b(s5_ind_cal, "beta", c(TRUE, FALSE)) - s5_b(s5_ind_not, "beta", c(TRUE, FALSE)))), 3)`
(`r f(max(abs(s5_b("fgee_fpca_wildL", "beta", c(TRUE, FALSE)) - s5_b("fgee_fpca_wildL_noT", "beta", c(TRUE, FALSE)))), 3)` with FPCA),
but the adjustment strongly affects the mean with 40 curves, where it sits at the floor on up to
`r f(100 * max(s5_bc("mean", c(TRUE, FALSE), "at_floor", 40)), 0)`% of the replicates of a setting. There, the
intervals for the mean are up to `r f(max(s5_b(s5_ind_cal, "mean", c(TRUE, FALSE), "wr", 40)), 2)` times as
wide as REML + CL2's, with an interval score up to
`r f(max(s5_b(s5_ind_cal, "mean", c(TRUE, FALSE), "sr", 40)), 2)` times that of REML + CL2, and cover
`r rng(s5_b(s5_ind_cal, "mean", c(TRUE, FALSE), g = 40))`. Without the adjustment, they cover
`r rng(s5_b(s5_ind_not, "mean", TRUE, g = 40))` under dependent errors at
`r rng(s5_b(s5_ind_not, "mean", TRUE, "wr", 40))` times REML + CL2's width and
`r rng(s5_b(s5_ind_not, "mean", FALSE, g = 40))` under independent errors at
`r rng(s5_b(s5_ind_not, "mean", FALSE, "wr", 40))` times that width. With 100 curves, the two versions
differ by at most `r f(max(abs(s5_b(s5_ind_cal, c("beta", "mean"), c(TRUE, FALSE), g = 100) - s5_b(s5_ind_not, c("beta", "mean"), c(TRUE, FALSE), g = 100))), 3)` in coverage.
For $\alpha$ and $\gamma$, the calibrated intervals cover
`r rng(s5_b(c("fgee_independent_wild", "fgee_ar1_wild", "fgee_fpca_wild"), c("alpha", "gamma"), TRUE))`
under dependence. These results concern a use of fastFGEE's bootstrap routine that its interface does
not offer, for targets other than those of its own function-on-scalar setting studied above.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s4-fgee-mse
#| tbl-cap: "Main factorial settings: paired MSE ratios on identical datasets (ratio of mean squared errors over replicates, grid-averaged), ranges over settings. fGEE: independence working correlation. In brackets: number of settings whose 95% replicate-bootstrap interval lies entirely below one / entirely above one."
s5_ct <- c(fgee_ind_vs_reml = "fGEE / REML", ncv_vs_reml = "NCV / REML", fgee_ind_vs_ncv = "fGEE / NCV")
s5_BP |>
  filter(contrast %in% names(s5_ct)) |>
  group_by(estimand, dep, contrast) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    txt = sprintf("%s [%d/%d]", rng(est), sum(upper < 1), sum(lower > 1)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = contrast, values_from = txt) |>
  mutate(estimand = factor(estimand, names(s5_estimands))) |>
  arrange(estimand, desc(dep)) |>
  mutate(
    estimand = ifelse(duplicated(estimand), "", s5_estimands[as.character(estimand)]),
    dep = ifelse(dep, "dependent", "independent")
  ) |>
  select(estimand, dep, n, all_of(names(s5_ct))) |>
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "",
    col.names = c("Estimand", "Errors", "Settings", unname(s5_ct)))
```

Under dependent errors, the one-step update reduces the mean squared error of $\beta$ relative to REML
(`r rng(s5_bp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta", TRUE)$est)`), by less than curve-blocked NCV
(`r rng(s5_bp("ncv_vs_reml", "beta", TRUE)$est)`): the ratio fGEE/NCV is
`r rng(s5_bp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta", TRUE)$est)`, with every bootstrap interval above one (lowest
lower bound `r f(min(s5_bp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta", TRUE)$lower), 2)`). Choosing, after the fact,
the working correlation with the lowest mean squared error in each setting gives a ratio of
`r rng(s5_bp("fgee_best_vs_ncv", "beta", TRUE)$est)`. Under independent errors, the ratio fGEE/REML for
$\beta$ is `r rng(s5_bp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta", FALSE)$est)`, above one in the settings with
$G = 40$ (`r rng(s5_bp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta", FALSE)$est[s5_bp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta", FALSE)$G == 40])`).
For $\alpha$ and $\gamma$, the ratio fGEE/NCV is `r rng(s5_bp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", c("alpha", "gamma"), c(TRUE, FALSE))$est)`.

### Plasmode datasets

The plasmode comparison uses the six datasets with independent source curves (observed curves
independent across subjects), the midpoint truth (refit at
the geometric mean of the REML and NCV smoothing parameters), the REML residual curves attached
to their own subjects with signs flipped per curve, all subjects and 40 subjects,
`r min(s5_P$R)` replicates per combination, and the plasmode study's own datasets; methods and interval
definitions are those of the main factorial settings (Gaussian responses). For the two cardiology datasets,
only aggregate results are reported. Monte Carlo standard errors of coverage are at most
`r f(max(s5_P$coverage_mc_se), 3)`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-s4-fgee-p
#| fig-cap: "Plasmode datasets (midpoint truth, REML residuals), β(s,t), per dataset and number of subjects G. Left: grid-averaged coverage of nominal 95% pointwise intervals (REML model-based and REML + CL2; fGEE Wald intervals from its covariance under the independence, AR(1) and FPCA working correlations; dashed: 0.95). Right: paired ratios of mean squared errors with 95% replicate-bootstrap intervals, fGEE with independence working correlation (log scale; dashed: equal error). Values: S7."
#| fig-height: 4.3
sfig_fgee_p(s5_P, s5_PP, s5_apps)
```

Over the `r nrow(distinct(s5_P, app, G))` combinations of dataset and number of subjects $G$, REML + CL2 covers $\beta(s,t)$ at
`r rng(s5_p("reml_cl2", "beta"))`, the mean at `r rng(s5_p("reml_cl2", "mean"))`, $\alpha(t)$ at
`r rng(s5_p("reml_cl2", "alpha"))` and $\gamma(t)$ at `r rng(s5_p("reml_cl2", "gamma"))`; model-based
REML intervals cover $\beta$ at `r rng(s5_p("reml_model", "beta"))` (@fig-s4-fgee-p). The fastFGEE 0.2.2 Wald
intervals cover $\beta$ at `r rng(s5_p(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "beta"))`
with SE/SD `r rng(s5_p(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "beta", "se_sd_ratio"))`
(REML + CL2: `r rng(s5_p("reml_cl2", "beta", "se_sd_ratio"))`), the mean at
`r rng(s5_p(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "mean"))`, $\alpha$ at
`r rng(s5_p(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "alpha"))` and $\gamma$ at
`r rng(s5_p(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "gamma"))`, the lowest values for the
randomized treatment effect in the AF trial
(`r rng(s5_p(c("fgee_independent", "fgee_ar1", "fgee_fpca"), "gamma", apps = "af"))`). With
calibrated critical values, the intervals for $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ cover
`r rng(s5_p(c("fgee_independent_wild", "fgee_ar1_wild", "fgee_fpca_wild"), c("alpha", "gamma")))`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s4-fgee-cal-p
#| tbl-cap: "Plasmode datasets (midpoint truth, REML residuals), β(s,t) and the mean: grid-averaged coverage (cov.) of nominal 95% pointwise intervals and 5% quantile of pointwise coverage (q05) for REML + CL2 with the normal critical value (CL2) and for fGEE (independence working correlation) with its calibrated critical value with its t adjustment (t) and without it (no t); width and interval score of the fGEE intervals relative to REML + CL2."
s5_P |>
  filter(estimand %in% c("beta", "mean"), method %in% c("reml_cl2", s5_ind_cal, s5_ind_not)) |>
  mutate(kind = c(reml_cl2 = "cl2", fgee_independent_wildL = "t", fgee_independent_wildL_noT = "no")[method]) |>
  select(estimand, app, G, kind, coverage, pointwise_q05, wr, sr) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = kind, values_from = c(coverage, pointwise_q05, wr, sr)) |>
  mutate(
    app = factor(app, names(s5_apps)),
    estimand = factor(estimand, c("beta", "mean"))
  ) |>
  arrange(estimand, app, desc(G)) |>
  mutate(
    app_lab = s5_apps[as.character(app)],
    app_lab = ifelse(duplicated(paste(estimand, app)), "", app_lab),
    estimand = ifelse(duplicated(estimand), "", s5_estimands[as.character(estimand)]),
    across(where(is.numeric) & !G, \(x) f(x, 2))
  ) |>
  select(estimand, app_lab, G, coverage_cl2, pointwise_q05_cl2, coverage_t, pointwise_q05_t, wr_t, sr_t,
    coverage_no, pointwise_q05_no, wr_no, sr_no) |>
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "", align = "llrrrrrrrrrrr",
    col.names = c("", "Dataset", "G", "CL2 cov.", "CL2 q05", "t cov.", "t q05", "t width", "t score",
      "no t cov.", "no t q05", "no t width", "no t score")) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 7, latex_options = "hold_position")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-s4-fgee-satt-p
#| tbl-cap: "The plasmode datasets of the previous table against REML + CL2 with the Satterthwaite critical value: its grid-averaged coverage (cov.) and 5% quantile of pointwise coverage (q05) for β(s,t), its coverage for the mean, and the width of the calibrated intervals for β(s,t) with and without the t adjustment as a multiple of its width."
s5_satt_p <- readr::read_csv("satterthwaite/summaries/satt-plasmode-cells.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(crit == "satt", truth == "MID", residual == "REML", estimand %in% c("beta", "mean")) |>
  select(app, G, estimand, coverage, pointwise_q05, width)
s5_w_t <- \(m) s5_P |> filter(method == m, estimand == "beta") |> select(app, G, w = width)
s5_satt_p |>
  filter(estimand == "beta") |>
  left_join(s5_satt_p |> filter(estimand == "mean") |> select(app, G, cov_mean = coverage), by = c("app", "G")) |>
  left_join(s5_w_t(s5_ind_cal), by = c("app", "G"), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  rename(w_t = w) |>
  left_join(s5_w_t(s5_ind_not), by = c("app", "G"), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  filter(!is.na(w_t)) |>
  mutate(app = factor(app, names(s5_apps)), wr_t = w_t / width, wr_no = w / width) |>
  arrange(app, desc(G)) |>
  mutate(
    app_lab = s5_apps[as.character(app)],
    app_lab = ifelse(duplicated(app), "", app_lab),
    across(c(coverage, pointwise_q05, cov_mean, wr_t, wr_no), \(x) f(x, 2))
  ) |>
  select(app_lab, G, coverage, pointwise_q05, cov_mean, wr_t, wr_no) |>
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, linesep = "", align = "lrrrrrr",
    col.names = c("Dataset", "G", "cov. beta", "q05 beta", "cov. mean", "t width", "no t width")) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(font_size = 8, latex_options = "hold_position")
```

Plasmode errors are residual curves with independent random signs, the same distribution as the
multipliers of the wild bootstrap, so this design resembles the bootstrap's own resampling scheme.
With all subjects and independence working correlation, the calibrated intervals cover $\beta$ at
`r rng(s5_p(s5_ind_cal, "beta", all_subj = TRUE))` (5% quantile of pointwise coverage
`r rng(s5_p(s5_ind_cal, "beta", "pointwise_q05", all_subj = TRUE))`; REML + CL2 with the normal
critical value `r rng(s5_p("reml_cl2", "beta", all_subj = TRUE))` and
`r rng(s5_p("reml_cl2", "beta", "pointwise_q05", all_subj = TRUE))`), at
`r rng(s5_p(s5_ind_cal, "beta", "wr", all_subj = TRUE))` times the width and
`r rng(s5_p(s5_ind_cal, "beta", "sr", all_subj = TRUE))` times the interval score of REML + CL2
(@tbl-s4-fgee-cal-p).

With 40 subjects, the $t$ adjustment sits at the floor on
`r rng(100 * s5_pc("beta", FALSE, "at_floor"), 0)`% of the replicates for $\beta$ and
`r rng(100 * s5_pc("mean", FALSE, "at_floor"), 0)`% for the mean. The intervals for $\beta$ then cover
`r rng(s5_p(s5_ind_cal, "beta", all_subj = FALSE))` at
`r rng(s5_p(s5_ind_cal, "beta", "wr", all_subj = FALSE))` times REML + CL2's width, and, without the
adjustment, `r rng(s5_p(s5_ind_not, "beta", all_subj = FALSE))` at
`r rng(s5_p(s5_ind_not, "beta", "wr", all_subj = FALSE))` times that width
(`r rng(s5_p(s5_all_not, "beta", all_subj = FALSE))` over the three working correlations).

For the mean,
the intervals without the adjustment cover `r rng(s5_p(s5_ind_not, "mean", all_subj = TRUE))` with all
subjects and `r rng(s5_p(s5_ind_not, "mean", all_subj = FALSE))` with 40, at
`r rng(s5_p(s5_ind_not, "mean", "wr"))` times REML + CL2's width. With the adjustment, they are up to
`r f(max(s5_p(s5_ind_cal, "mean", "wr", all_subj = FALSE)), 2)` times as wide with 40 subjects and up to
`r f(max(s5_p(s5_ind_cal, "mean", "wr", all_subj = TRUE)), 2)` times with all subjects: the floor also
applies to the `r s5_P_ALL[["ecg_roahd"]]` subjects of the ECG 8-lead data, whose bases have more coefficients
(`r f(100 * s5_pc("mean", TRUE, "at_floor", apps = "ecg_roahd"), 0)`% of the replicates).

For $\beta$, the ratio fGEE/REML of mean squared errors is `r rng(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta")$est)`, below one
in `r sum(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta")$est < 1)` of `r nrow(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta"))`
combinations, with the interval below one in `r sum(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_reml", "beta")$upper < 1)`.
Against curve-blocked NCV, fGEE is worse in `r sum(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta")$lower > 1)` combinations,
better in `r sum(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta")$upper < 1)`
(`r paste(unique(s5_apps[s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta")$app[s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta")$upper < 1]]), collapse = ", ")`)
and not resolved in the remaining
`r sum(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta")$lower <= 1 & s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "beta")$upper >= 1)`;
the best working correlation per combination, chosen after the fact, gives a ratio fGEE/NCV of
`r rng(s5_pp("fgee_best_vs_ncv", "beta")$est)`. For $\gamma$, the ratio fGEE/NCV is
`r rng(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "gamma")$est)`, with the interval below one in
`r sum(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "gamma")$upper < 1)` combinations
(`r knitr::combine_words(unique(s5_apps[s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "gamma")$app[s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "gamma")$upper < 1]]))`)
and above one in `r sum(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "gamma")$lower > 1)`; for $\alpha$, it is
`r rng(s5_pp("fgee_ind_vs_ncv", "alpha")$est)`.
